subject.title: [Bug]: memory-core narrative generation silently produces no text and writes fallback diary entries (light/rem/deep phases)

question: Should the durable post-run read guarantee be implemented in the generic subagent/session lifecycle, or should memory-core own run-keyed polling and recovery?
rationale: Both approaches can address the symptom, but they establish different ownership and security boundaries; the open pull requests currently implement only plugin-local portions without resolving that architectural choice.

options.title: Fix the generic completion contract
options.body: Make successful run completion guarantee that the run’s assistant output is durably readable, then keep memory-core on the standard session API.

options.title: Add plugin-local recovery
options.body: Have memory-core poll by run identity and recover from a supported trajectory or archived-session API without changing generic completion semantics.

options.title: Land diagnostics separately
options.body: Merge the diagnostic improvement as a partial observability fix while keeping the root data-loss issue open for a separate lifecycle repair.

recommendation.title: Fix the generic completion contract
recommendation.body: Make successful run completion guarantee that the run’s assistant output is durably readable, then keep memory-core on the standard session API.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-core dreaming history and merge activity make this person the strongest available routing candidate for the owner-boundary decision.
